title: Windowed Off-Policy Expert Value-Agreement
subtitle: A cheap off-policy diagnostic: does a policy match the expert's windowed value from expert states?

sections.text: On a past task $i$, this measures whether a policy achieves the same windowed value as that task's expert, starting from states the expert actually reached. It answers can the new model play as well as the expert? without paying for many full-episode rollouts and without letting easy early-game play inflate the score. It is NOT a standalone forgetting metric: it conditions on expert-reached states and says nothing about whether the policy can REACH them on its own. It is reported ALONGSIDE the on-policy no-op anchor (greedy-100), never instead of it. VERIFICATION: the implementation PASSED code-verifier against the design doc.

Shared by both procedures: discount $\gamma$ and sign-clip flag (= task.clip\_rewards). $\mathrm{clip}(r)=\mathrm{sign}(r)\in\{-1,0,+1\}$ if clipping else $r$ (matches the training value scale). The windowed value over $n$ steps is $V_\mathrm{win}=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\gamma^j\,\mathrm{clip}(r_j)$; the raw window score is $\sum r_j$. Greedy action $=\arg\max$ over the head's logits. The SNAPSHOT ENVIRONMENT (make\_snapshot\_env) is preprocessing-only: base ALE (frameskip 1, full 18-action set) wrapped by AtariPreprocessing (skip / max-pool, grayscale, resize to $84\times84$), emitting a SINGLE frame. It has NO frame-stack, NO TimeLimit, NO reward clip, and terminal-on-life-loss forced OFF, so the evaluator manages the 4-frame stack itself and a restored mid-episode state is not spuriously terminated. It requires sticky-actions off for bit-exact clone/restore.
Procedure 1: build the expert state set (once per task, reusable)

Precomputed ONCE per task and reused across every checkpoint and method (the dominant cost saving). A window is CONSEQUENTIAL iff its raw score $\ge$ consequential-thresh (expert scored non-trivially) AND its discounted-clipped value $V^*_\mathrm{win}\ge v_\mathrm{floor}$ (so the relative-shortfall denominator is bounded away from 0). The adaptive horizon $H_i$ is the smallest grid $H$ with $\ge\tau$ consequential windows; this and the consequential filter together avoid the $0\approx 0$ vacuity of sparse Atari games.

sections.name: build-expert-state-set(expert, task)
inputs: expert policy $\pi_i^*$ (greedy source of states); task $i$ (game, $\gamma$, frame-stack $\mathrm{fs}$, clip)
$n_\mathrm{starts}=20$ no-op starts; cap $N=5000$ kept states; rng seed
outputs: ExpertStateSet: game, task-id, horizon $H_i$, $\gamma$, $\mathrm{fs}$, clip, list of ExpertState, meta
each ExpertState: ale-state, stacked-obs, $V^*_\mathrm{win}$, raw-win, $n_\mathrm{win}$, steps-to-term, category (pickled)

body.text: (A) ROLL the expert and snapshot every visited state:
for $k=1,\dots,n_\mathrm{starts}$ do
env $\leftarrow$ snapshot-env; frame $\leftarrow$ env.reset(seed $+\,k$)   (no-op start diversity)
stack $\leftarrow$ deque of $\mathrm{fs}$ copies of the first frame   (frame-stack reset semantics)
while not done and steps $<$ cap do
obs $\leftarrow$ stack as $(\mathrm{fs},84,84)$ oldest..newest
$a \leftarrow$ greedy expert action on obs;   $s_t \leftarrow$ ale.cloneState()   (SNAPSHOT BEFORE stepping)
frame, $r$, term, trunc $\leftarrow$ env.step$(a)$;   record $(s_t,\ \mathrm{obs},\ r)$;   push frame
record whether the trajectory TRULY terminated (vs hit the step cap)
(B) ADAPTIVE horizon:  window$(i,t,H)$ caps at steps-to-terminal, returns $(V^*_\mathrm{win},\ \mathrm{raw},\ n_\mathrm{win})$
consequential$(V^*_\mathrm{win},\mathrm{raw}) \equiv (\mathrm{raw}\ge \mathrm{thresh})$ and $(V^*_\mathrm{win}\ge v_\mathrm{floor})$
$\mathrm{frac}(H) \leftarrow$ fraction of ALL $(i,t)$ starts whose $H$-window is consequential
$H_i \leftarrow$ smallest $H\in G$ with $\mathrm{frac}(H)\ge\tau$   (else $\max G$, record a warning)
(C) COLLECT consequential candidates at $H_i$, then sample:
for each trajectory $i$ and start $t$: $(V^*_\mathrm{win},\mathrm{raw},n_\mathrm{win}) \leftarrow$ window$(i,t,H_i)$
if not consequential: skip   (keep ONLY consequential states)
category $\leftarrow$ near-terminal if (truly-terminated and steps-to-term $\le H_i$),  else early if $t<20$,  else mid
append ExpertState$(s_t,\ \mathrm{obs}_t,\ V^*_\mathrm{win},\ \mathrm{raw},\ n_\mathrm{win},\ \mathrm{steps\_to\_term},\ \mathrm{category})$
if kept $> N$: keep a uniform random subset of size $N$ (no replacement); pickle the set

sections.text: REMARK: cloneState / restoreState are O(1), replacing seed + action-prefix replay that would cost an entire episode for a near-terminal state. The snapshot is taken BEFORE env.step, so a stored $s_t$ pairs with the obs the expert acted on and the reward $r_t$ that action produced. The frame stack is reconstructed exactly from the stored obs; it is never snapshotted through the ALE core.
Procedure 2: evaluate expert agreement (per checkpoint, per task)

Restores each expert state (O(1)) and rolls the POLICY greedily for that state's stored $n_\mathrm{win}$ steps (the SAME window length the expert's $V^*_\mathrm{win}$ covered, so the returns are strictly equal-horizon, capped at terminal). Reports the ONE-SIDED shortfall: the expert is the ceiling, so beating it is not penalized (hinged at 0), mirroring the training hinge $[\hat V_k^L-\hat V_k^G]_+$ of Part A. States are processed in banks of $n_\mathrm{envs}$ snapshot envs run synchronously.

sections.name: evaluate-expert-agreement(policy, task, state-set, task-id)
inputs: policy; task-id (the head to evaluate); precomputed state-set (supplies $H,\gamma,\mathrm{fs}$, clip)
$n_\mathrm{envs}=8$ snapshot envs as a synchronous bank
outputs: lower is better; 0 $\Rightarrow$ policy matches or beats the expert on every kept state

body.text: if state-set empty: return NaN gaps, $n$-states $=0$
create $n_\mathrm{envs}$ snapshot envs; reset each once (seed 0) to init ALE before any restore
for each chunk of up to $B=n_\mathrm{envs}$ states do
for lane $j$, expert state $s$: ale$_j$.restoreState$(s)$; sync stale life counter; seed stack$_j$ from stored obs
$V^\pi_j\leftarrow 0$;  $g_j\leftarrow 1$;  done$_j\leftarrow$ false;  window length $w_j\leftarrow s.n_\mathrm{win}$
for step $=0,\dots,\max_j w_j - 1$ (break if all done) do
acts $\leftarrow$ batched greedy POLICY actions on stacks at task-id
for each active lane $j$:
if step $\ge w_j$: mark done$_j$ (reached the expert window length); continue
frame, $r$, term, trunc $\leftarrow$ env$_j$.step(acts$_j$)
$V^\pi_j \leftarrow V^\pi_j + g_j\cdot\mathrm{clip}(r)$;   $g_j\leftarrow g_j\cdot\gamma$;   slide stack$_j$ (drop oldest, append frame)
if term or trunc: mark done$_j$   (cap at terminal)
for lane $j$, expert state $s$:  gap $\leftarrow \max(0,\ s.V^*_\mathrm{win}-V^\pi_j)$;  rel $\leftarrow$ gap$/s.V^*_\mathrm{win}$
record gap, rel, and rel under $s$.category
return mean gap, mean rel, $n$-states, $H$, per-category mean rel
